turns.t: Doctor, it's the blurred vision when I'm reading. The words go all fuzzy and I'm terrified it's the start of something awful, like going blind.
Righto, let's slow down. When did the blurring first start?
About three months ago, give or take.
Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
It's worse in the evenings, under the lamp. In the morning it's not so bad. Is that a bad sign?
Not necessarily. Think of it like a camera lens getting smudged.  Does anything make it better?
Holding the page further away helps a bit.
Okay, that's useful. What about the eyes themselves, how do they feel?
Tired. My eyes feel tired by the evening, like I've been staring too long, even when I haven't.
Mm-hm. Any headaches that go with it?
I did get headaches in the first month, behind the eyes. But they've gone now. I haven't had one in weeks.
Good, so that part has settled. Have you seen any flashing lights, or a curtain coming across your vision?
No, nothing like that. No flashes. Oh, goodness, would that be worse?
It would be a reason to come in straight away, so I'm glad you haven't. Now, you've been in before for your regular reviews. Run me through what you're on at the moment.
Well, I'm on the metformin, 500 milligrams twice a day, for the diabetes. Then there's the ramipril, 5 milligrams every morning, for my blood pressure.
Okay, and anything else?
Yes, sorry, the atorvastatin, 40 milligrams at night, for the cholesterol.
Good on her. And just so I've got it right, the diabetes and blood pressure have both been going a while?
The diabetes about nine years now. The blood pressure I've had even longer.
No one's pointing fingers. Let's see what we're dealing with. Have you had any trouble with your heart or chest? Chest pain, puffing on the stairs?
No, nothing there.
That's good to hear. Now, about smoking. Do you smoke at all?
No, I stopped smoking about ten years ago.
That's a great effort. I'll check your pressure first, and then we'll look at the eyes.
Pressure is 142 over 86, and your pulse is 72 beats per minute.
Is that high? It's always high at the doctor's, it's the nerves.
It's a bit up, but not alarming, and nerves can do that. I'll keep an eye on it. Now, look straight ahead for me, and I'll shine a light in each eye.
Like this? Should I keep them open the whole time?
Perfect. Your pupils react equally to the light, just what I like to see.

I can see some slight cloudiness in the lens of both eyes, like a window that's got a bit of fog on it. And at the back of the eye there's no bleeding, which is one thing I was keen to check, with your diabetes.
Cloudiness? That sounds terrible. Is it a cataract?
From what I can see, this looks like early cataracts. That's the lens clouding over slowly, common as we get older.
So that's what the blurry reading is?
That's my best guess at this stage. But I wouldn't put all the weight on it yet. High sugars can also blur things on their own, so I want to rule that part in or out.
How? What do I need to do?
First, I'd like to get a blood test called HbA1c, that tells us your average sugar over the last three months.
Right. I'm a bit scared of what it will say.
Whatever it says, we can work with it. And second, I'd like to arrange retinal photographs, where we take a picture of the back of both eyes.
Does that hurt? Do they put drops in?
The drops sting for a few seconds, that's all. They make the light too bright afterwards, so bring someone to drive you home.
In the meantime, use a brighter light for reading, and take a break from the phone every half hour or so.
I'll do that. Will the cataract go away on its own?
No, it won't, unfortunately. If it gets in the way of your life, there's a simple operation to swap the cloudy lens for a clear one. But there's no rush.
That's a relief. I thought you'd say straight away.
No rush at all. Once I've got the blood results and the photos, I'd like you back in four weeks, so we can go over it all together and decide on the next step.
Four weeks. And what if it gets worse before then?
Then ring us and we'll get you in earlier. And flashing lights or a curtain across your eye means come straight in, same day.
Straight in, got it. Thank you, doctor, you've taken a weight off my mind.
No worries at all. Mind the step on the way out.
Thanks. See you in four weeks, then.
Take care.

chief_complaint.value: the blurred vision when I'm reading

social_history.details: I stopped smoking about ten years ago

physical_examination.finding: slight cloudiness in the lens of both eyes

clinical_actions.description: Use brighter light for reading and take regular phone breaks
